column1: # boru Language Specification: every variant of `each` (and its side-effecting
# twin `for-each`) as REAL programs spell them.
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# Family: each-variants. Written to widen the corpus past the one-liner
# shapes it had — over lists, maps and strings; with a literal body, a
# def-bound body, a fn value, a lambda and a closure; nested; inside a fn;
# defining locals; calling user fns; producing compound values; over
# computed and empty collections; with an index; and chained into another
# each or a fold.
# EVERY row's expected column is the engine's own answer, captured from
# `boru do <input> end canon` — the same canon rendering the spec runner
# compares against.
# ROWS THAT REFUSE TO COMPILE ARE RECORDED DELIBERATELY, as OPEN DEFECTS.
# They are collected in §18 and each note carries the exact reason
# `BORU_FORCE_COMPILE=1` printed. They are not mistakes and must not be
# deleted to make a ceiling green: they are the gap between the corpus and
# real code that this family exists to make visible.
# `each` has NO String signature — `each [f] 'abc'` is a signature_error —
# so the string rows here walk the characters the way real code does, by
# splitting first (§13, §15).
# §1  each over a LIST with a literal code body
each [mul 2] [1 2 3]
column3: forward form: body first, collection second

column3: stack form: the collection is already on the stack

column3: the body may use stack words

column3: a longer stack body: square, then double

column1: each [size] ['aa' 'bbb']

a list of Floats

column3: a heterogeneous list under a code body

column3: a body that grows each element into a list
a body that shrinks each element
ten elements — the body is compiled once and driven per element
